title: Round625: request-only player-view conversion in Ninjask Batch
status: prototype throughput measured; current PPO not connected
format: Local Champions Reg M-C doubles with open-team-sheet rule removed

method.view_source: incremental per-player Battle.log plus that player's current request

throughput.comparison_note: The previous Ninjask numeric-only random loop measured 8171.5 games/s. Round602f full Showdown PPO rollouts measured 37.63 games/s, but these are not like-for-like: this probe excludes current-policy feature mapping, inference, PPO updates, and writes. The 3.0x ratio to that rollout rate is only an investigation signal, not a demonstrated speedup.

interpretation: Redacted log/request trackers retain the richer JSON view and match Batch OBS/IDS encodings exactly in 20,380 decision rows. Parsing that view reduced the random-policy Batch rate by about 98.6% relative to numeric-only Batch, but the remaining 114 games/s is still a promising ceiling for an eventual feature adapter. This is not current-policy training throughput and does not yet establish that the present model's full inputs can be reconstructed.
next: Map the player Tracker.view into the existing model inputs without dropping volatile/history features; compare reconstructed features against local Showdown records; only then attach the checkpoint, measure complete CPU/CUDA rollout throughput, and decide whether a JAX simulator is justified.
limitations: Random legal actions only; no PPO action scoring, current checkpoint, conversion to project features, data writing, or learner update.
CPU only; no GPU game simulation or model inference was measured.
This is a throughput probe, not a strength result, full mechanics certification, or direct comparison with Showdown training throughput.
